full_judgment: 12. It is now a settled proposition that a writ petition may be dismissed on the ground of inordinate and unsatisfactorily explained delay on the part of the petitioner. Article 102 of the Constitution does not provide for any period of limitation for filing writ petition; however, the Courts have, on public policy ground, consistently taken the view that delay defeats relief under Article 102 of the Constitution. In the event of inordinate and unsatisfactorily explained delay, the High Court Division may dismiss any application under Article 102 of the Constitution and this is regardless of the merit. Thus in course of hearing any application under Article 102 of the Constitution, this Division, before entering into the merit of the application is required to first ascertain whether there had been inordinate delay in filing the application and if so, whether the delay had been satisfactorily explained. In the event the inordinate delay is not satisfactorily explained, this Division is entitled refuse the writ petitioner relief.
